A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ND-CNPFuse, and their main text, equations, figures, and tables are readable. However, both end after the references on page 10 and omit the cited appendices A-C. This prevents verification of appendix-only derivations, configurations, and experiments, including newly referenced evaluations in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original four-dataset fusion evaluations, runtime measurements, neuron simulations, parameter sensitivity experiments, and ablations in Tables 1-4 and Figures 2 and 5-8.

after.justification: v3 retains original fusion evaluations and ablations, updates evaluated comparators, and reports additional C++ timing and an energy estimate.

M1.justification: The available method description retains SML preprocessing, coupled-neuron iteration, neighborhood aggregation of spike counts, decision-map comparison, and pixelwise fusion. Time reindexing and the C++ implementation do not establish an algorithm change. Detailed parameter rules referred to Appendix A.2 cannot be compared.

E1.justification: The documented fusion coverage remains Lytro, MFFW, MFI-WHU, and Real-MFF, with the same respective counts of 20, 13, 120, and 710 image pairs. v3 newly references downstream salient-object detection and noisy-input evaluation, but the cited Appendices C.2 and C.4 are absent, preventing verification of added task or scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 and Figures 5-6 replace ZMFF and MGDN with CCF and Mask-DiFuser, retaining seven other fusion comparators. This is a bounded revision of the comparison set. v3 also mentions an LIF comparison, but its results are assigned to missing Appendix C.3 and cannot be verified.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 extends the coupling-radius sweep from {2, 4, 8, 16, 32} to include zero. v3 adds C++ runtime evaluation and an energy estimate for 520-by-520 Lytro images. The main dataset counts, six fusion metrics, hardware assignments, selected radius of 16, and 110 iterations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds a zero-radius control to the existing neighborhood sensitivity analysis. The neurodynamic and SML ablations and Lytro failure-case study remain. v3 claims an additional noisy-input analysis in Appendix C.4, but its evidence is unavailable and cannot substantiate a broader robustness expansion.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. Figure 7 already contains shaded bands in v1; v3 retains this presentation without adding an explanation of their statistical meaning.

E6.justification: All 24 ND-CNPFuse scores in Table 1 remain unchanged, while comparator rows and rankings change: the MFFW exception shifts from PSNR to SSIM. Table 2 adds 0.18 seconds for C++ alongside the retained 0.41 seconds for MATLAB; Section 5.2 adds 1.12e-5 J per pair. Table 3 revises percentage gains, including FMIw from 17.09% to 17.29%, and Table 4 changes without-SML PSNR from 26.987 to 26.983.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the synaptic-input definition from K(i) using Pkl(t-1) to K(n) using Pkl(n). Corollary 1 changes its bound from strict to non-strict inequality. The linear-decay relation is explicitly identified as an approximation. The four theorems and principal continuous-firing threshold remain; appendix derivations are unavailable.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same principal contributions: CNP neurodynamic analysis, training-free interpretable decision maps without post-processing, and state-of-the-art results on four datasets. The claimed average improvement over baseline CNP remains 5.73%. Removing 'generalizable' from the conclusion does not withdraw the generalization claim repeated elsewhere.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations that the tested radius and iteration settings are universal, SML benefits noisy inputs, and the C++ runtime satisfies real-time MFIF requirements. The low-contrast-edge explanation is retained but attached to the SSIM shortfall instead of PSNR, following the changed comparator set. The noisy-input explanation lacks its referenced appendix evidence.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly states that comparators use official code and weights and reports an implemented C++ version where v1 only suggested a future port. It supplies image dimensions for the energy estimate. Hardware and the project-code link remain unchanged; appendix-only parameter configuration details are unavailable.

R1.justification: Related work adds explicit diffusion-model coverage and correctly groups the already-cited Mask-DiFuser there. Six references are added, covering CCF, VDMUFusion, Text-DiFuse, nonlinear spiking P-system fusion, SpikingJelly, and energy calculation. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged; bibliographic updates to existing works are not new citations.

P1.justification: v3 locally streamlines related work, proof explanations, and experimental discussion while retaining the same section sequence and narrative. It replaces the third-generation-network description with biological inspiration wording, adds two authors, and revises affiliations and an acknowledgement identifier. These are limited editorial changes.

P2.justification: Figures 3-4 are redrawn, Figures 5-6 update and reorder comparator panels, and Figure 7 extends its radius axis to zero. Table 1 consolidates method labels and adds publication tags; Table 2 displays dual implementation runtimes. The eight figures, four tables, and overall two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity and evidential support through corrected mathematical statements, an explicit approximation, a zero-radius control, and reported C++ timing replacing v1's speculative efficiency claim. These gains are limited: fusion scores are unchanged, comparator replacement removes MGDN's stronger MFFW PSNR result, and missing appendices prevent crediting the claimed downstream and noise evaluations.
